issues.body: `build_field` sets `iri_only` for only the singleton `sh:IRI` case, then applies it solely in the `None if iri_only` match arm. When the same property has `sh:datatype`, `sh:class`, or `sh:node`, the node-kind requirement is discarded. For example, `sh:datatype xsd:string; sh:nodeKind sh:IRI` is unsatisfiable, but lowering emits a scalar String field whose generated loader accepts an `xsd:string` literal. Other node-kind sets fall through the wildcard arm and become unconstrained when no other source exists. This is the same wrong-acceptance defect reported in round 5 and contradicts the documented guarantee that constraints which cannot be modeled faithfully produce `SchemaError`.
issues.fix_hint: Represent node-kind requirements in the lowering constraint accumulator and conjoin them with datatype/class/node requirements. Return a typed `SchemaError` whenever the conjunction cannot be faithfully enforced; do not discard it. Add an end-to-end generated-loader test for contradictory `sh:datatype xsd:string` plus `sh:nodeKind sh:IRI` that proves lowering fails closed (or that nonconforming values are rejected), and add coverage for supported or explicitly rejected non-IRI node-kind constraints.
issues.title: Combined sh:nodeKind constraints are still silently dropped

verdict.summary: Round 6 is stagnant: the round-5 major correctness issue remains. `build_field` records only the singleton `sh:nodeKind sh:IRI` case in `iri_only`, and uses it only when no datatype/class/node source exists. Consequently a combined constraint such as `sh:datatype xsd:string; sh:nodeKind sh:IRI` lowers to a String scalar and the generated loader accepts a literal even though the conjunction is unsatisfiable. Other node-kind sets are still ignored as well. The new tests cover only standalone `sh:nodeKind sh:IRI`; none exercises conjunction or non-IRI node kinds, so the advertised fail-closed faithful-lowering contract is not established.
